title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction: Header: page 1, 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)', box 'GF VI', dated 18 June 1986. Grothendieck states his plan. Before defining a 'contrée' (an axiomatic space-like object), he will first define a 'contrée avec notion de multistrates'. In it, a chosen family of 'multistrates' plays the role of a family of open sets generating a topology, or of a generating family of objects of a topos. This is a basis or site-generator: the space is to be presented by a privileged class of tame pieces. To do this he starts Part I, 'Algèbre de figures' or 'Atelier' (workshop). An algebra of figures consists first of three sets: L (lieux, loci), M (multistrates) and F (figures). They are related by various maps and each carries various structures. There are canonical injections L ↪ M ↪ F, labelled b) and a). These let one regard a locus as a special multistrate and a multistrate as a special figure, so L ⊂ M ⊂ F. He announces two further pairs of maps. The next page shows what they are: (a) an incidence map F ↪ P(M), F ↦ F̃ = Depl(F), the 'déploiement' or set of incident multistrates; (b) the induced map F → Fig(M) ⊂ P(P(M)), F ↦ {X̃ : X ∈ F̃}. M carries an order ≤ with X̃ = {Y ≤ X}, and F̃ is a closed (down-closed) part of M. In modern terms the combinatorial skeleton looks like this: M is a poset, as for a poset of strata ordered by closure or the face poset of a cell decomposition. Multistrates correspond to principal down-sets, i.e. closures. Figures are certain down-closed subsets, i.e. closed sets in the Alexandrov topology of M, and so are 'constructible' unions of pieces. Loci are a distinguished subclass. The overall aim (Analysis situs) is an axiomatic tame topology in which spaces are built from such combinatorial-incidence data rather than from point-set topology. This continues the 'topologie modérée' programme of the Esquisse (1984).
errors: No mathematical errors on this page; it is purely definitional and programmatic. Gap: the 'diverses structures' on L, M, F and the precise nature of 'lieux' are not yet specified here.

ideas.what: Presenting a space ('contrée') by a privileged generating family of 'multistrates', analogous to a basis of opens or a generating family of a topos
ideas.modern_name: basis of a topology / generating family of a site; tame (stratified) presentation of spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Grothendieck SGA4 for generating families of topoi)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 (generating families); the tame-topology motivation is in Esquisse d'un programme §5

ideas.what: 'Algèbre de figures' / 'Atelier': a triple of sets of loci, multistrates and figures with injections L ⊂ M ⊂ F and an incidence relation between figures and multistrates
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology via incidence structures; closest analogues are o-minimal structures (definable sets) and poset/Alexandrov models of stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1984–86); stratified posets: MacPherson, Lurie, Barwick–Glasman–Haine
ideas.where_published: Only the general call for 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this specific formalism appears unpublished

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins an axiomatic 'Analysis situs' in which a space ('contrée') is given by an 'atelier' of loci ⊂ multistrates ⊂ figures. Multistrates generate the space like a basis or a topos generating family. This is a concrete attempt at the tame-topology foundations called for in the Esquisse, independent of o-minimality, and it seems not to have been studied or developed.
missed.quote: la famille des multistrates choisies jouant un peu le rôle d'une famille d'ouverts engendrant une topologie, ou une famille génératrice d'éléments d'un topos
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may give a combinatorial/incidence-theoretic alternative to o-minimal structures for tame topology. It could connect to current poset-based treatments of stratified spaces (exit paths, exodromy), where a stratified space is governed by its poset of strata.

missed.claim: On this and the next page, multistrates form a poset, multistrates are principal down-sets, and figures are down-closed sets. Combined with the topos analogy, this implicitly links tame/stratified topology to Alexandrov topologies on posets and to topos-theoretic generation. Modern stratified homotopy theory (stratifications over posets) makes this link only later and without reference to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: ou une famille génératrice d'éléments d'un topos
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is historically relevant to the genesis of 'stratified spaces as objects over posets' and to the Esquisse's tame-topology programme.

deep.surprise_reason: First page of an unpublished 1986 manuscript that sets up a novel axiomatic vocabulary (contrée, multistrate, figure, atelier) for tame topology. It is interesting as an unexplored foundational attempt, but this page is only definitional set-up with no results.
transcription_corrections: 'et elles-mêmes[?] munies de diverses structures' should read 'et chacun munis de diverses structures'.
In 'famille d'ouverts', the struck words appear to be 'baignant' and 'pris', replaced by 'engendrant' written above; confirmed reading: 'une famille d'ouverts engendrant une topologie'.
'Atelier' is underlined, with its initial letter overwritten.
